newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK short-date paper yields fall on keen demand.
newsitem.headline: HK short-date paper yields fall on keen demand.

text.p: Hong Kong short-date Exchange Fund bill yields eased on Tuesday on keen demand as traders were building up their portfolios ahead of the start of Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) on December 9, dealers said.
"Demand on bills is very keen and the extra HK$5.0 billion bills tendered earlier cannot satisfy buyers," a local bank dealer said.

The special issue, the first of two 28-day tenders to facilitate the implementation of RTGS, was 2.7 times oversubscribed. Dealers said the average accepted yield of 4.78 percent was lower than expected.

"This probably will further depress short-date bill yields when the market reopens after lunch," the local bank dealer said, adding that one-month Exchange Fund bills yielded 4.86 percent in the secondary market at noon.
One-week note yield fell about 10 points to 4.87 percent.

Banks were collecting Exchange Fund bills and notes because under the RTGS system the paper can be used to obtain interest-free intraday liquidity by carrying out intraday repurchase transactions with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
Longer dated notes taking the lead of U.S. treasuries were relatively steady.
Three-year notes yielded 6.04 percent versus 6.06 on Monday. Seven-year notes yielded 6.90 percent versus 6.89 and 10-year note yield was 7.14 percent versus 7.15.
In the interbank rate market, overnights fell sharply with plenty of offers seen in the morning session following the HKMA's hefty money injection on Monday, dealers said.
"Traders tried to lend in the morning on fears that overnight rates would fall significantly in the afternoon when banks are more comfortable to lend," a dealer said.
Overnight rates eased to 4-7/8 3/4 percent from 5-1/8 1/16 and three-month was steady at 5-17/32 15/32.
